target_customer: Engineering teams at SaaS and analytics companies running PostgreSQL who need to scale out, for multi-tenant apps and real-time analytics
problem: Scaling a relational database beyond one machine meant giving up transactions, joins and foreign keys or rebuilding on NoSQL.
business_model: Open source Postgres extension with paid enterprise software and a managed database service (Citus Cloud, 2016)

founders.name: Ozgun Erdogan
founders.background_notes: Conceived the idea while working on NoSQL data architectures.

founders.name: Sumedh Pathak
founders.role: Co-founder (YC page lists founder and engineer)

founders.name: Umur Cubukcu
founders.background_notes: Business side, from consulting; technical flag inferred from role at BCG only.

competitors.what: SQL on Hadoop engine based on Google Dremel
competitors.traction_then: Described by TechCrunch as similar to CitusDB at its Feb 2013 launch

competitors.name: Apache Drill
competitors.what: Open source SQL on Hadoop engine based on Google Dremel
competitors.traction_then: Named in the same TechCrunch launch coverage

competitors.name: Pivotal Greenplum
competitors.traction_then: A 451 Group note flagged its open source push as a threat to becoming the default MPP Postgres

competitors.name: Vertica, Teradata Aster, Amazon Redshift
competitors.traction_then: Listed by the 451 Group as other MPP databases Citus faced

technical_complexity.rationale: Building a distributed query engine on top of PostgreSQL, later as an unforked extension that tracks every Postgres release, is deep database engineering.

defensibility.rationale: Hard to replicate technically and data-resident customers face high switching costs, but the engine became open source and cloud providers could offer alternatives.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Greenplum and Hadoop engines crowded the space in 2013; in January 2019 Microsoft bought Citus Data, with terms undisclosed, for its Azure Postgres offering.

market_need_then: By 2012 to 2013 SQL on Hadoop was crowded and fast moving, and the founders wanted scale-out SQL that kept transactions, joins and foreign keys.

branding.domain_note: Uses citusdata.com, not citus.com; the exact .com was not obtained.

identity.logo: Elicorn icon, described only by its label on the site
identity.mascot_or_character: Elicorn, an elephant and unicorn style character implied by its name (not confirmed by a source)
identity.voice_and_tone: Plain engineering tone: Distributed Postgres. At any scale.

branding.community_and_virality: Donated 1% of stock to PostgreSQL non-profits in November 2018; open source project has about 10,100 GitHub stars.

brand_strength.rationale: Distinctive name and mascot with strong open source community goodwill, though not a household brand.

pivots.to: CitusDB analytics database for Hadoop data
pivots.why: Positioned as real-time SQL analytics over HDFS using Postgres foreign data wrappers; reasons not stated.

pivots.to: Open source Postgres extension, plus Citus Cloud in July 2016
pivots.why: Company says it unforked Citus and made it an extension to track Postgres releases.

outcome_analysis: Citus Data began in the Summer 2011 YC batch as scale-out SQL, launched CitusDB for Hadoop in 2013 into a crowded SQL-on-Hadoop field, then in 2016 unforked and open sourced Citus as a Postgres extension and launched a cloud service. It raised a $9.5M Series A led by Khosla in October 2015 and was acquired by Microsoft in January 2019, with terms undisclosed. The extension strategy and Postgres community goodwill explain the positive exit.
notes: Seed: Global Venturing reports a $1.6M seed in 2012 from Digital Garage, Trinity Ventures and angels, while an aggregator lists $2.0M in June 2013; conflicting and single source each, so not recorded as a round. Series A amount comes from the company timeline link and secondary reports; Data Collective participation from secondary reports. Total raised estimates range from $11.1M to over $13M. Founders' technical flag for Cubukcu is a judgment. Elicorn expansion not confirmed by a source.
